Task: Outline and partially script a 15-minute educational video on climate change.

15-Minute Educational Video: “Climate Change—Causes, Impacts, Solutions”

Target audience
• High-school students & general public (ages 14+)  
• Assumes no prior scientific background

Learning objectives
1. Define climate change and distinguish it from weather.  
2. Explain the major human and natural drivers.  
3. Describe at least four observable impacts (physical, ecological, social).  
4. Identify individual, community, and policy-level solutions.  
5. Inspire viewers to take one concrete climate action.

Overall structure (15:00)
0:00–0:45 Cold-open hook  
0:45–1:30 Intro & roadmap  
1:30–4:00 Section 1: “What Is Climate Change?”  
4:00–7:00 Section 2: “Why Is It Happening?”  
7:00–10:00 Section 3: “What Are the Impacts?”  
10:00–13:00 Section 4: “What Can We Do?”  
13:00–14:30 Section 5: Hope & Success Stories  
14:30–15:00 Call to Action & Outro

Visual language
• Combination of presenter on camera, motion graphics, quick expert sound bites, and short field footage (wildfires, wind turbines, youth activists).  
• Color palette: warm oranges/reds for problem; cool greens/blues for solutions.  
• Consistent icon set (thermometer, CO₂ cloud, glacier, solar panel, megaphone).

--------------------------------------------------------------------
PARTIAL SCRIPT (first ~5 minutes fully scripted, remainder in detailed beats)
--------------------------------------------------------------------

COLD-OPEN HOOK (0:00-0:45)
[Video: Montage—burning wildfires, flooded city streets, then kids planting trees]
SFX: Heartbeat builds underneath.

HOST (V.O.)
“From record-breaking heatwaves to once-in-a-century storms that now come every other year, our planet is sending us an urgent message.”

[Cut to Host on camera, standing in a mixed urban-nature backdrop.]

HOST
“I’m Jamie Rivera, and in the next 15 minutes we’re going to unpack what’s driving these changes— and, more important, what we can do about it.”

TITLE SLATE: “CLIMATE CHANGE—CAUSES, IMPACTS, SOLUTIONS”

INTRO & ROADMAP (0:45-1:30)
[Simple animated timeline appears beside host.]

HOST
“We’ll start by clearing up exactly what climate change is, look at why it’s happening so fast, explore the impacts already unfolding, and finish with proven solutions you can join today.”

[Quick pop-ups of section icons.]

SECTION 1 — WHAT IS CLIMATE CHANGE? (1:30-4:00)

1:30–2:15 Defining climate vs. weather
[Graphic: Two panels; left shows daily weather icons flipping; right shows 30-year average temperature line.]

HOST
“Think of weather as your mood and climate as your personality—one is day-to-day, the other is the long-term pattern.”

2:15–3:10 Evidence the climate is warming
[Visual: NASA global temperature anomaly map time-lapse.]

HOST (picture-in-picture with graph)
“Earth’s average surface temperature has risen about 1.1 °C since the late 19th century. That may sound tiny, but remember: the difference between today’s world and the last Ice Age was only about 5 °C.”

3:10–4:00 How scientists know
[Split-screen: ice cores, tree rings, satellite data.]

HOST
“Multiple, independent lines of evidence—ice-core bubbles, tree rings, ocean buoys, and satellites—all point to the same trend: rapid warming, especially in the past 70 years.”

SECTION 2 — WHY IS IT HAPPENING? (4:00-7:00)

4:00–4:40 The greenhouse effect basics
[Animation: Sunlight enters, infrared heat bounces, some trapped by CO₂ layer.]

HOST (gesturing to animation)
“Greenhouse gases are like the glass walls of a garden greenhouse. They’re essential for life—but we’ve thickened that glass.”

4:40–5:25 Human contributions
[Graphic pie chart: CO₂ = 76 %, CH₄ = 16 %, N₂O = 6 %, etc.]

HOST
“Burning coal, oil, and natural gas adds about 37 billion tons of CO₂ to the air each year. Deforestation and industrial farming add methane and nitrous oxide.”

5:25–6:15 Natural factors vs. human fingerprint
[Overlay: Volcano vs. fossil-fuel curve comparison.]

HOST
“Volcanoes do emit CO₂, but human industry emits 100 times more annually. And if the Sun were the culprit, we’d see both the upper and lower atmosphere warming—yet satellites show the stratosphere cooling while the surface heats up. That’s the signature of greenhouse gases.”

6:15–7:00 Short recap transition
[Quick on-screen quiz: “Biggest human source of CO₂? A) Transportation B) Electricity & Heat C) Cement” (highlight correct answer: B).]

HOST
“Okay, we know the ‘why.’ Next, let’s see what that means for people and the planet.”

--------------------------------------------------------------------
DETAILED BEATS (7:00–15:00)
--------------------------------------------------------------------

SECTION 3 — WHAT ARE THE IMPACTS? (7:00–10:00)

7:00–7:50 Physical systems  
• Melting Arctic sea ice, sea-level rise animation (3.6 mm/yr).  
7:50–8:40 Ecosystems & biodiversity  
• Coral bleaching footage, shifting animal ranges map.  
8:40–9:20 Human health & economies  
• Heat-stress infographic, crop yield drop overlay.  
9:20–10:00 Equity lens  
• Map showing that lowest-emission countries are often highest-risk.

SECTION 4 — WHAT CAN WE DO? (10:00–13:00)

10:00–10:45 Personal actions  
• Graphics of diet shift, energy efficiency, voting.  
10:45–11:45 Community & city-level  
• Bike lanes B-roll, community solar garden drone shot.  
11:45–12:45 National & global policy  
• Paris Agreement icon, Inflation Reduction Act money flow schematic.  
12:45–13:00 Rapid recap (kinetic text): “Electrify, Decarbonize, Protect Forests, Adapt.”

SECTION 5 — HOPE & SUCCESS STORIES (13:00–14:30)

13:00–13:45 Case study: Denmark’s 50 % wind-powered grid.  
13:45–14:15 Youth climate lawsuit success in Montana.  
14:15–14:30 Quote on screen (“The future is not written.”) transition to call to action.

CALL TO ACTION & OUTRO (14:30–15:00)

HOST on camera, back to opening location (now sunrise lighting):
“Pick one action—just one—today. Whether that’s swapping a car trip for a bike ride or emailing your representative about clean energy, multiply it by millions of us and we bend the curve.”

[On-screen QR code to resources page.]

TEXT: “Learn more • Take action • Share this video”  
LOGO + fade out.

--------------------------------------------------------------------
Production notes
--------------------------------------------------------------------
Music
• Underscore: light electronic ambient for data; acoustic hopeful track for solutions.  
Color grading
• Warm tone for problems, cool/bright for solutions to evoke hope.  
Captioning & accessibility
• Burn-in open captions; audio descriptions script.  
Expert cameos (10-second bites)
• Glaciologist Dr. Aisha Tan (Impacts section).  
• Climate policy analyst Mateo Chen (Solutions section).

B-roll sources
• NASA public-domain imagery.  
• Unsplash, Pexels (CC0) for renewable energy shots.
